WeatherVision - Complete Assignment 1 and Assignment 2¶

Rakhman Seidigali · SE-2411 · Computer Vision, Astana IT University
Instructor: Nurym Kaiyrkhan

This notebook contains the project's implemented data preparation, models, training, evaluation, augmentation ablation, Grad-CAM, occlusion validation and application integration. Assignment 1 compares Simple CNN and MobileNetV2; Assignment 2 adds ConvNeXt-Tiny. All reported experimental results come from the completed runs.

Demonstration mode is the default: it verifies and displays existing artifacts and runs small checkpoint-based examples without training or replacing official outputs. Full reproduction is optional: set RUN_FULL_REPRODUCTION = True in Part 0 to train the four configurations into a separate directory. The longer training, full-test and occlusion branches are clearly gated. Code cells define and use notebook-local implementations; none import project algorithms from src.

The notebook can be opened in the repository or copied into Google Colab. Photographs, trained weights and measured artifacts remain external data, not embedded model binaries. Missing artifacts are obtained from the pinned public repository and model release; the first standalone run needs internet access and downloads about 221 MiB of checkpoints plus the dataset. The displayed execution was performed locally, not on hosted Colab.

Part 0 - Environment Setup¶

Use a Python 3.11+ kernel and the repository's existing environment locally. In a fresh Colab runtime, set INSTALL_PACKAGES = True once and run the installation cell before the imports. The requirements below match the project runtime. CPU inference is the default for the small demonstrations; optional training detects CUDA, Apple MPS or CPU automatically.

def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(path).open("rb") as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()


def write_json(path: Path, value) -> None:
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Reject NaN/Infinity so machine-readable results remain standards compliant.
    text = json.dumps(value, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", dir=path.parent, delete=False) as f:
        f.write(text + "\n")
        tmp = f.name
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def seed_everything(seed: int = 42) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)
    # Small image datasets suffer from CPU thread oversubscription.
    torch.set_num_threads(min(4, os.cpu_count() or 1))


def select_device(name: str = "auto") -> torch.device:
    if name == "auto":
        name = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else (
            "mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")
    if name not in {"cpu", "cuda", "mps"}:
        raise ValueError("Device must be auto, cpu, cuda, or mps")
    if name == "cuda" and not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise ValueError("CUDA requested but unavailable")
    if name == "mps" and not torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        raise ValueError("MPS requested but unavailable")
    return torch.device(name)


def synchronize(device: torch.device) -> None:
    if device.type == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
    elif device.type == "mps":
        torch.mps.synchronize()


def environment(device=None) -> dict:
    import torchvision
    import sklearn
    return {
        "python": platform.python_version(), "torch": str(torch.__version__),
        "torchvision": str(torchvision.__version__), "sklearn": sklearn.__version__,
        "numpy": np.__version__, "platform": platform.platform(),
        "processor": platform.processor(), "cpu_count": os.cpu_count(),
        "device": str(device or select_device()),
        "cuda_available": torch.cuda.is_available(),
        "mps_available": torch.backends.mps.is_available(),
        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else None,
        "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
    }

def save(fig, path):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor="white", dpi=300)
    plt.close(fig)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Experiment:
    model: str
    epochs: int = 6
    batch_size: int = 16
    lr: float = 0.001
    weight_decay: float = 0.0001
    patience: int = 4
    augment: bool = True
    pretrained: bool = True
    freeze_backbone: bool = True
    seed: int = 42
    image_size: int = 224
    num_workers: int = 0
    device: str = "auto"

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.model not in {"cnn", "mobilenet", "convnext"}:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown architecture: {self.model}")
        for name in ("epochs", "batch_size", "patience", "seed", "image_size", "num_workers"):
            if type(getattr(self, name)) is not int:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be an integer")
        if min(self.epochs, self.batch_size, self.patience) < 1 or self.lr <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Epochs, batch size, patience, and learning rate must be positive")
        if self.image_size != 224:
            raise ValueError("This protocol fixes image_size=224 for pretrained preprocessing")
        if self.num_workers < 0 or self.seed < 0 or self.weight_decay < 0:
            raise ValueError("Workers, seed, and weight decay cannot be negative")
        for name in ("augment", "pretrained", "freeze_backbone"):
            if type(getattr(self, name)) is not bool:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be true or false, not a string")
        if self.device not in {"auto", "cpu", "cuda", "mps"}:
            raise ValueError("Invalid device")
        if self.model == "cnn" and (self.pretrained or self.freeze_backbone):
            raise ValueError("The CNN baseline must train from scratch without freezing")

    def to_dict(self):
        return asdict(self)


def load_config(path: Path) -> dict[str, Experiment]:
    raw = yaml.safe_load(Path(path).read_text())
    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not isinstance(raw.get("experiments"), dict):
        raise ValueError("Config requires an experiments mapping")
    allowed = {f.name for f in fields(Experiment)}
    common = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k != "experiments"}
    if set(common) - allowed:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown shared settings: {set(common) - allowed}")
    result = {}
    for run, values in raw["experiments"].items():
        if not isinstance(run, str) or not run.replace("_", "").isalnum():
            raise ValueError("Run names may only contain letters, numbers, and underscores")
        result[run] = Experiment(**(common | values))
    if not result:
        raise ValueError("At least one experiment is required")
    return result


def validate_ablation(a: Experiment, b: Experiment) -> None:
    differences = {k for k in a.to_dict() if a.to_dict()[k] != b.to_dict()[k]}
    if a.model != "convnext" or b.model != "convnext" or differences != {"augment"}:
        raise ValueError("ConvNeXt ablation configurations must differ only in augmentation")

EXPERIMENTS_YAML = """
seed: 42
image_size: 224
num_workers: 0
device: auto
experiments:
  cnn_baseline:
    model: cnn
    epochs: 12
    batch_size: 32
    lr: 0.001
    weight_decay: 0.0001
    patience: 4
    augment: true
    pretrained: false
    freeze_backbone: false
  mobilenet_improved:
    model: mobilenet
    epochs: 8
    batch_size: 32
    lr: 0.001
    weight_decay: 0.0001
    patience: 4
    augment: true
    pretrained: true
    freeze_backbone: true
  convnext_aug:
    model: convnext
    epochs: 6
    batch_size: 16
    lr: 0.001
    weight_decay: 0.0001
    patience: 4
    augment: true
    pretrained: true
    freeze_backbone: true
  convnext_noaug:
    model: convnext
    epochs: 6
    batch_size: 16
    lr: 0.001
    weight_decay: 0.0001
    patience: 4
    augment: false
    pretrained: true
    freeze_backbone: true
"""
configuration_document = yaml.safe_load(EXPERIMENTS_YAML)
shared_configuration = {key: value for key, value in configuration_document.items() if key != "experiments"}
configs = {run: Experiment(**(shared_configuration | settings))
           for run, settings in configuration_document["experiments"].items()}
validate_ablation(configs["convnext_aug"], configs["convnext_noaug"])
seed_everything(42)
device = select_device(DEMO_DEVICE)

Official artifacts and availability¶

Only data, configurations, figures and result files are fetched from the pinned revision; no Python implementation is downloaded or executed. Hash validation prevents silent artifact substitution. Existing files are verified and left in place. A separate release downloader restores the full trained checkpoints, including their pretrained backbones. The implementation source hashes identify the canonical source revision from which the visible definitions were copied.

def ensure_artifacts(paths):
    for relative in paths:
        target = (ROOT / relative).resolve()
        if not target.is_relative_to(ROOT.resolve()):
            raise ValueError("Artifact path escapes the working directory")
        expected = ASSET_SHA256[relative]
        if not target.is_file():
            if not FETCH_MISSING_ASSETS:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing artifact: {relative}; enable FETCH_MISSING_ASSETS or install it locally.")
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            temporary = target.with_suffix(target.suffix + ".download")
            try:
                url = f"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/commedeschamps/WeatherVision/{SOURCE_REVISION}/{relative}"
                request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "WeatherVision-notebook/1"})
                with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response, temporary.open("wb") as stream:
                    shutil.copyfileobj(response, stream)
                if sha256_file(temporary) != expected:
                    raise ValueError(f"Artifact hash mismatch: {relative}")
                temporary.replace(target)
            finally:
                temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        if sha256_file(target) != expected:
            raise ValueError(f"Existing artifact differs from the official snapshot: {relative}")


ensure_artifacts(list(ASSET_SHA256))
In [6]:
def sha256(path):
    with Path(path).open('rb') as stream:
        return hashlib.file_digest(stream, 'sha256').hexdigest()


def download_asset(asset, destination):
    destination = Path(destination)
    if destination.is_file() and sha256(destination) == asset['sha256']:
        return 'verified existing'
    if destination.exists():
        raise ValueError(f'Existing file has a different checksum: {destination}. Move it aside before downloading.')
    if not asset['url'].startswith('https://github.com/commedeschamps/WeatherVision/releases/download/'):
        raise ValueError('Checkpoint URL must identify the WeatherVision release.')
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = None
    try:
        request = urllib.request.Request(asset['url'], headers={'User-Agent': 'WeatherVision-checkpoint-setup/1'})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=destination.parent, suffix='.download', delete=False) as target:
                temporary = Path(target.name)
                total = 0
                while block := response.read(1024 * 1024):
                    total += len(block)
                    if total > asset['bytes']:
                        raise ValueError('Checkpoint exceeds expected size')
                    target.write(block)
        if temporary.stat().st_size != asset['bytes'] or sha256(temporary) != asset['sha256']:
            raise ValueError('Downloaded checkpoint failed size/SHA-256 validation')
        os.replace(temporary, destination)
        return 'downloaded and verified'
    finally:
        if temporary is not None:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    if not destination.is_file() and not FETCH_MISSING_ASSETS:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing trained checkpoint for {asset['run']}")
    download_asset(asset, destination)

Part 1 - Dataset Acquisition¶

The source is Gbeminiyi Ajayi's Multi-class Weather Dataset for Image Classification (2018, Mendeley Data V1, CC BY 4.0), accessed through the resized PerceptiLabs mirror. The exact mirror commit is pinned below. The implementation rejects unsafe archive paths, symlinks and oversized members, checks image decoding and converts images to RGB after EXIF orientation. The existing source photographs are reused when present.

In [7]:
ALIASES = {"cloud": "cloudy", "cloudy": "cloudy", "rain": "rain", "shine": "shine", "sunrise": "sunrise"}
EXTENSIONS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".webp", ".tif", ".tiff"}
MIRROR_REPO = "PerceptiLabs/Weather-Analysis"
MIRROR_COMMIT = "ad78ac8fcf1b1aae229ca6e5310aa75b06783787"

def safe_extract(archive: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
    """Reject traversal, symlinks, oversized members, and ZIP bombs before writing."""
    destination = Path(destination).resolve()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as z:
        total = 0
        for member in z.infolist():
            name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
            mode = member.external_attr >> 16
            total += member.file_size
            if (name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or "\\" in member.filename
                    or stat.S_ISLNK(mode) or member.file_size > 100_000_000
                    or total > 2_000_000_000):
                raise ValueError(f"Unsafe ZIP member: {member.filename}")
            target = (destination / member.filename).resolve()
            if not target.is_relative_to(destination):
                raise ValueError("ZIP path escapes destination")
        destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        z.extractall(destination)
In [8]:
def download(url: str, path: Path) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    part = path.with_suffix(".part")
    try:
        request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "WeatherVision/1.0"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response, part.open("wb") as f:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, f)
        part.replace(path)
    finally:
        part.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def obtain_dataset(data_dir: Path, local_zip: Path | None = None,
                   source_dir: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    data_dir = Path(data_dir)
    raw = data_dir / "raw"
    provenance_path = data_dir / "source.json"
    if source_dir is not None:
        if not Path(source_dir).is_dir():
            raise ValueError(f"Dataset directory does not exist: {source_dir}")
        write_json(provenance_path, {"type": "local_directory", "source": str(Path(source_dir).resolve()),
                                    "original_doi": "10.17632/4drtyfjtfy.1"})
        return Path(source_dir).resolve()
    if raw.exists() and any(raw.rglob("*")):
        if local_zip:
            raise ValueError("Raw data already exists; use a new --data-dir for a different archive")
        return raw
    archive = data_dir / "downloads" / "weather.zip"
    if local_zip:
        archive = Path(local_zip).resolve()
        provenance = {"type": "manual_zip", "archive_name": archive.name}
    else:
        if archive.exists() and provenance_path.exists():
            provenance = json.loads(provenance_path.read_text())
            if sha256_file(archive) != provenance.get("archive_sha256"):
                raise ValueError("Cached archive hash differs from source.json")
        else:
            try:
                commit = MIRROR_COMMIT
                url = f"https://codeload.github.com/{MIRROR_REPO}/zip/{commit}"
                download(url, archive)
                provenance = {"type": "public_mirror", "repository": MIRROR_REPO,
                              "commit": commit, "url": url}
            except Exception as e:
                raise RuntimeError("Automatic download failed. Download the Mendeley or GitHub ZIP, "
                                   "then run prepare --local-zip /path/weather.zip. " + str(e)) from e
    provenance.update(archive_sha256=sha256_file(archive), original_doi="10.17632/4drtyfjtfy.1",
                      attribution="Gbeminiyi Ajayi (2018); CC BY 4.0",
                      mirror_note="PerceptiLabs mirror images are resized; not an asserted byte-identical original")
    # Failed extraction never leaves a partially populated raw/ cache.
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=data_dir) as staging:
        safe_extract(archive, Path(staging) / "raw")
        shutil.move(str(Path(staging) / "raw"), raw)
    write_json(provenance_path, provenance)
    return raw
In [9]:
def infer_label(path: Path, source: Path) -> str | None:
    relative = path.relative_to(source)
    labels = {ALIASES[p.lower()] for p in relative.parts[:-1] if p.lower() in ALIASES}
    if len(labels) > 1:
        raise ValueError(f"Conflicting class directories: {relative}")
    if labels:
        return next(iter(labels))
    # Original archives can contain flat names such as cloudy001.jpg.
    stem = path.stem.lower()
    for prefix in sorted(ALIASES, key=len, reverse=True):
        suffix = stem[len(prefix):].lstrip("_- ")
        if stem.startswith(prefix) and suffix.isdigit():
            return ALIASES[prefix]
    return None


def open_rgb(path) -> Image.Image:
    with Image.open(path) as image:
        return ImageOps.exif_transpose(image).convert("RGB")

Part 2 - Dataset Cleaning¶

The actual preparation implementation is below. It verifies decoding, computes file and decoded-pixel SHA-256, pHash and dHash, and forms connected duplicate groups before splitting. Near candidates require both hash distances ≤4, absolute log-aspect-ratio difference ≤0.10 and thumbnail RGB RMSE ≤0.12. Conflicting-label groups are quarantined; repeated decoded images are removed. No generated photographs enter the training set.

Demonstration mode reads the original audit: 1,123 valid images, 26 removed exact duplicates and 1,097 retained photographs. Optional rebuilding writes a separate audit and must reproduce the fixed manifest; it never replaces the official split.

In [11]:
def dataset_figures(frame, root, directory):
    counts = pd.crosstab(frame.label, frame.split).reindex(index=CLASSES, columns=["train", "val", "test"])
    counts.to_csv(directory / "class_distribution.csv")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 3.5), layout="constrained")
    counts.plot.bar(ax=ax, color=COLORS[:3], rot=0)
    ax.set(xlabel="Visual category", ylabel="Retained images", title="Shared dataset membership")
    ax.legend(title="Split", frameon=False)
    save(fig, directory / "class_distribution.png")
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(9, 4.7), layout="constrained")
    for j, label in enumerate(CLASSES):
        # Training-only inspection avoids using test imagery during model design.
        subset = frame[(frame.label == label) & (frame.split == "train")].head(2)
        for i in range(2):
            axes[i, j].axis("off")
            if i < len(subset):
                row = subset.iloc[i]
                axes[i, j].imshow(open_rgb(root / row.path))
                axes[i, j].set_title(f"{label.title()} · train", fontsize=9)
    save(fig, directory / "inspection.png")
In [12]:
def prepare_dataset(source: Path, data_dir: Path, root: Path = ROOT, seed: int = 42) -> pd.DataFrame:
    source, data_dir, root = Path(source).resolve(), Path(data_dir), Path(root).resolve()
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows, corrupt, ignored, thumbnails = [], [], [], []
    for path in sorted(source.rglob("*")):
        if not path.is_file() or path.suffix.lower() not in EXTENSIONS:
            continue
        label = infer_label(path, source)
        if label is None:
            ignored.append(str(path.relative_to(source)))
            continue
        try:
            with Image.open(path) as image:
                image.verify()
            image = open_rgb(path)
            width, height = image.size
            if min(width, height) < 16:
                raise ValueError("Image shorter side is below 16 pixels")
            pixels = hashlib.sha256(f"{width}x{height}:".encode() + image.tobytes()).hexdigest()
            rows.append({"path": path.relative_to(root).as_posix(), "label": label,
                         "class_id": CLASS_TO_IDX[label], "width": width, "height": height,
                         "sha256": sha256_file(path), "pixel_sha256": pixels,
                         "phash": str(imagehash.phash(image)), "dhash": str(imagehash.dhash(image))})
            thumbnails.append(np.asarray(image.resize((16, 16)), dtype=np.float32) / 255)
        except (OSError, ValueError, Image.DecompressionBombError) as e:
            corrupt.append({"path": str(path), "error": str(e)})
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("No recognized, valid weather images found")
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    parent = list(range(len(frame)))

    def find(i):
        while parent[i] != i:
            parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]
            i = parent[i]
        return i

    def union(i, j):
        parent[find(j)] = find(i)

    pairs = []
    for i in range(len(rows)):
        for j in range(i):
            a, b = rows[i], rows[j]
            exact = a["sha256"] == b["sha256"] or a["pixel_sha256"] == b["pixel_sha256"]
            p = (int(a["phash"], 16) ^ int(b["phash"], 16)).bit_count()
            d = (int(a["dhash"], 16) ^ int(b["dhash"], 16)).bit_count()
            aspect = abs(math.log((a["width"] / a["height"]) / (b["width"] / b["height"])))
            rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((thumbnails[i] - thumbnails[j]) ** 2)))
            near = p <= 4 and d <= 4 and aspect <= 0.10 and rmse <= 0.12
            if exact or near:
                union(i, j)
                pairs.append({"path_a": a["path"], "path_b": b["path"], "label_a": a["label"],
                              "label_b": b["label"], "kind": "exact" if exact else "near",
                              "phash_distance": p, "dhash_distance": d, "rgb_rmse": rmse})
    group_ids = {}
    for i in range(len(rows)):
        group_ids.setdefault(find(i), []).append(rows[i]["pixel_sha256"])
    frame["group"] = [min(group_ids[find(i)])[:20] for i in range(len(rows))]
    conflicts = set(frame.groupby("group").filter(lambda x: x.label.nunique() > 1).group)
    frame["status"] = "retained"
    frame.loc[frame.group.isin(conflicts), "status"] = "quarantined_label_conflict"
    eligible = frame.status == "retained"
    repeated = frame.loc[eligible].duplicated("pixel_sha256")
    frame.loc[repeated[repeated].index, "status"] = "exact_duplicate_removed"
    manifest = assign_splits(frame[frame.status == "retained"].drop(columns="status"), seed)
    validate_manifest(manifest, root)
    frame.to_csv(data_dir / "image_audit.csv", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(corrupt, columns=["path", "error"]).to_csv(data_dir / "corrupted_images.csv", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(pairs, columns=["path_a", "path_b", "label_a", "label_b", "kind", "phash_distance", "dhash_distance", "rgb_rmse"]).to_csv(data_dir / "duplicate_pairs.csv", index=False)
    manifest.to_csv(data_dir / "manifest.csv", index=False)
    stats = {"seed": seed, "valid_images_before_dedup": len(frame), "corrupt_images": len(corrupt),
             "ignored_unrecognized_images": ignored, "retained_images": len(manifest),
             "exact_duplicates_removed": int((frame.status == "exact_duplicate_removed").sum()),
             "quarantined_conflicts": int((frame.status == "quarantined_label_conflict").sum()),
             "duplicate_pairs": len(pairs), "near_duplicate_pairs": sum(p["kind"] == "near" for p in pairs),
             "independent_groups": int(manifest.group.nunique()),
             "counts": pd.crosstab(manifest.label, manifest.split).to_dict(),
             "manifest_sha256": sha256_file(data_dir / "manifest.csv"),
             "near_duplicate_rule": "pHash<=4 AND dHash<=4 AND abs(log(aspect ratio ratio))<=0.10 AND RGB thumbnail RMSE<=0.12",
             "limitations": "Detected duplicate components cannot cross splits. Conservative hashes can miss transformed copies; manually review duplicate_pairs.csv and inspection figures. Mirror may differ from original dataset."}
    # Convert pandas/numpy scalars to portable JSON scalars.
    write_json(data_dir / "statistics.json", json.loads(json.dumps(stats, default=int)))
    dataset_figures(manifest, root, data_dir)
    return manifest

Part 3 - Train / Validation / Test Split¶

Training fits the weights, validation selects the checkpoint and stopping point, and the test set estimates final performance. Seed 42 is a fixed reproducibility choice, not an accuracy advantage. Grouped splitting prevents detected duplicates from crossing partitions. All four models use the same manifest: 768 train, 164 validation and 165 test images. The split is not regenerated during demonstration.

In [14]:
def assign_splits(frame: pd.DataFrame, seed: int = 42) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Approximate class-stratified 70/15/15 allocation of indivisible groups."""
    frame = frame.copy()
    if frame.groupby("group").label.nunique().max() > 1:
        raise ValueError("Conflicting labels within a duplicate group must be quarantined")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    frame["split"] = "train"
    for label in CLASSES:
        sizes = frame[frame.label == label].groupby("group", sort=True).size()
        if len(sizes) < 3:
            raise ValueError(f"{label}: need at least 3 independent groups to split")
        groups = list(rng.permutation(sizes.index.to_numpy()))
        target = max(1, round(sizes.sum() * 0.15))
        for split, reserve in (("val", 2), ("test", 1)):
            chosen, count = [], 0
            # Whole groups are selected until closest to the image-count target.
            while len(groups) > reserve:
                group = groups[0]
                if chosen and abs(count - target) <= abs(count + sizes[group] - target):
                    break
                chosen.append(groups.pop(0))
                count += int(sizes[group])
            frame.loc[frame.group.isin(chosen), "split"] = split
    validate_manifest(frame, check_files=False)
    return frame
In [15]:
def validate_manifest(frame: pd.DataFrame, root: Path = ROOT, check_files=True) -> None:
    required = {"path", "label", "class_id", "split", "group", "sha256", "pixel_sha256"}
    if not required.issubset(frame.columns) or frame.empty:
        raise ValueError("Manifest is empty or missing required columns")
    if frame[list(required)].isna().any().any():
        raise ValueError("Manifest contains missing identifiers")
    if set(frame.label) != set(CLASSES) or set(frame.split) != {"train", "val", "test"}:
        raise ValueError("All four classes and all three splits are required")
    if not (frame.label.map(CLASS_TO_IDX) == frame.class_id).all():
        raise ValueError("Class index mapping is inconsistent")
    if frame.path.duplicated().any():
        raise ValueError("Duplicate paths in manifest")
    for key in ("group", "sha256", "pixel_sha256"):
        if (frame.groupby(key).split.nunique() > 1).any():
            raise ValueError(f"Leakage across splits: {key}")
    if (frame.groupby("group").label.nunique() > 1).any():
        raise ValueError("Duplicate group contains conflicting labels")
    counts = pd.crosstab(frame.label, frame.split).reindex(index=CLASSES, columns=["train", "val", "test"], fill_value=0)
    if (counts == 0).any().any():
        raise ValueError("Every class must appear in each split")
    if check_files:
        for value in frame.path:
            path = (root / value).resolve()
            if not path.is_relative_to(root.resolve()) or not path.is_file():
                raise ValueError(f"Missing or unsafe manifest path: {value}")


def verify_content(frame: pd.DataFrame, root: Path = ROOT) -> None:
    validate_manifest(frame, root)
    for row in frame.itertuples():
        if sha256_file(root / row.path) != row.sha256:
            raise ValueError(f"Image content changed since preparation: {row.path}")

Part 4 - Image Preprocessing and Augmentation¶

Simple CNN and MobileNetV2 resize the shorter side to 256 pixels; ConvNeXt uses 236. All inputs receive a 224-square center crop, tensor conversion and ImageNet normalization with means [0.485, 0.456, 0.406] and standard deviations [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]. Training alone adds horizontal flips, rotation up to 8 degrees and mild brightness, contrast and saturation jitter. Validation and test use deterministic transforms. The example below applies the actual implementation to a training photograph with a fixed demonstration seed.

In [17]:
def resize_size(architecture: str) -> int:
    return 236 if architecture == "convnext" else 256


def transform(split="test", augment=False, architecture="cnn"):
    operations = [T.Resize(resize_size(architecture), interpolation=InterpolationMode.BILINEAR),
                  T.CenterCrop(224)]
    if split == "train" and augment:
        operations.extend([T.RandomHorizontalFlip(), T.RandomRotation(8),
                           T.ColorJitter(brightness=0.15, contrast=0.15, saturation=0.10)])
    operations.extend([T.ToTensor(), T.Normalize([0.485, 0.456, 0.406], [0.229, 0.224, 0.225])])
    return T.Compose(operations)

Part 5 - PyTorch Dataset and DataLoaders¶

WeatherDataset reads relative paths from the fixed manifest, applies the selected model's transform and returns an image tensor and integer class ID. Training shuffles with an independent, epoch-seeded generator; validation does not shuffle. Batch sizes are 32 for the A1 models and 16 for ConvNeXt. The loaders below demonstrate one training batch without updating any model.

In [19]:
class WeatherDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, frame: pd.DataFrame, root=ROOT, split="test", augment=False, architecture="cnn"):
        self.frame = frame[frame.split == split].reset_index(drop=True)
        self.root = Path(root)
        self.transform = transform(split, augment, architecture)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.frame)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        row = self.frame.iloc[index]
        return self.transform(open_rgb(self.root / row.path)), int(row.class_id)

Part 6 - Assignment 1: Simple CNN¶

The baseline learns three convolutional blocks from scratch. Each contains a 3×3 convolution, batch normalization, ReLU and max pooling. Global average pooling, dropout 0.25 and a four-output linear layer complete the network. The structure and shape table below use the genuine saved checkpoint; no random-weight classifier is used for reported results.

In [21]:
class SimpleCNN(nn.Module):
    """Three small convolutional blocks and global pooling; trained from scratch."""
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        layers = []
        channels = 3
        for out in (16, 32, 64):
            layers.extend([nn.Conv2d(channels, out, 3, padding=1, bias=False),
                           nn.BatchNorm2d(out), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(2)])
            channels = out
        self.features = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(nn.Flatten(), nn.Dropout(0.25), nn.Linear(64, 4))

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.classifier(self.pool(self.features(x)))

Part 7 - Assignment 1: MobileNetV2¶

MobileNetV2 uses inverted residuals, depthwise spatial filtering and linear bottlenecks. The shared construction function below is the actual project implementation for all three architectures. Fresh training requests official IMAGENET1K_V1 weights, replaces the head and freezes the pretrained parameters. Demonstration loads the full saved state, so it needs no additional pretrained download. Only the 1,280-to-4 head trains: 5,124 parameters. Frozen feature modules stay in evaluation mode during training.

In [23]:
def build_model(architecture: str, pretrained=True, freeze_backbone=True) -> nn.Module:
    if architecture == "cnn":
        model = SimpleCNN()
    elif architecture == "mobilenet":
        model = mobilenet_v2(weights=MobileNet_V2_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1 if pretrained else None)
        model.classifier[1] = nn.Linear(model.last_channel, 4)
    elif architecture == "convnext":
        model = convnext_tiny(weights=ConvNeXt_Tiny_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1 if pretrained else None)
        model.classifier[2] = nn.Linear(model.classifier[2].in_features, 4)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown architecture: {architecture}")
    if architecture != "cnn" and freeze_backbone:
        for parameter in model.parameters():
            parameter.requires_grad_(False)
        # Only the new linear head trains; ConvNeXt LayerNorm remains pretrained.
        head = model.classifier[1] if architecture == "mobilenet" else model.classifier[2]
        for parameter in head.parameters():
            parameter.requires_grad_(True)
    return model


def set_training_mode(model, architecture, freeze_backbone):
    model.train()
    if architecture != "cnn" and freeze_backbone:
        # Keep pretrained BatchNorm statistics and stochastic-depth behavior fixed.
        model.features.eval()


def parameter_counts(model):
    return {"parameters": sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()),
            "trainable_parameters": sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)}

Part 8 - Training Implementation¶

The following cells contain the complete loss/metric calculation, checkpoint validation, per-epoch forward/backward loop and training controller. Cross-entropy and AdamW optimize only parameters with gradients enabled. Validation macro-F1 selects checkpoints; ties retain the earlier epoch, and patience four controls stopping. Resume restores model/optimizer states and absolute epoch seeds. Checkpoint format and class order are unchanged.

The notebook port removes package-relative imports because the same definitions are already visible here. Training provenance records the canonical source hashes and identifies the notebook implementation, rather than trying to hash absent src/ files in standalone Colab. The optimization, augmentation, timing and selection algorithms are otherwise unchanged.

In [25]:
def calculate_metrics(y_true, y_pred):
    if len(y_true) == 0 or len(y_true) != len(y_pred):
        raise ValueError("Metric inputs must be nonempty and have equal length")
    if any(int(v) not in range(4) for v in list(y_true) + list(y_pred)):
        raise ValueError("Class indices must be in [0, 3]")
    p, r, f1, _ = precision_recall_fscore_support(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(4)), average="macro", zero_division=0)
    return {"accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)), "precision_macro": float(p),
            "recall_macro": float(r), "f1_macro": float(f1),
            "confusion_matrix": confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(4))).tolist(),
            "per_class": classification_report(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(4)), target_names=CLASSES,
                                               zero_division=0, output_dict=True)}
In [26]:
def atomic_checkpoint(path: Path, payload: dict):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = path.with_suffix(".tmp")
    torch.save(payload, temporary)
    os.replace(temporary, path)


def load_checkpoint(path, device="cpu"):
    device = torch.device(device)
    try:
        checkpoint = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    except (pickle.UnpicklingError, EOFError) as error:
        raise ValueError("Cannot decode checkpoint; download the project weights again") from error
    if not isinstance(checkpoint, dict) or checkpoint.get("format_version") != 1 or checkpoint.get("classes") != list(CLASSES):
        raise ValueError("Unsupported checkpoint format or class mapping")
    if not isinstance(checkpoint.get("config"), dict) or not isinstance(checkpoint.get("model_state"), dict):
        raise ValueError("Checkpoint metadata or model weights are missing")
    try:
        config = Experiment(**checkpoint["config"])
    except TypeError as error:
        raise ValueError("Malformed checkpoint configuration") from error
    # All weights are saved, so inference never downloads anything.
    model = build_model(config.model, pretrained=False, freeze_backbone=config.freeze_backbone)
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["model_state"], strict=True)
    model.to(device).eval()
    return model, checkpoint

def training_curves(history, path):
    frame = pd.DataFrame(history)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10, 2.65), layout="constrained")
    for ax, metric, label in zip(axes, ["loss", "accuracy", "f1_macro"], ["Loss", "Accuracy", "Macro-F1"]):
        for prefix, color in (("train", COLORS[0]), ("val", COLORS[1])):
            ax.plot(frame.epoch, frame[f"{prefix}_{metric}"], marker="o", markersize=3, color=color, label=prefix.title())
        ax.set(xlabel="Epoch", ylabel=label)
        if metric != "loss":
            ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
        ax.set_xticks(frame.epoch.iloc[::2] if len(frame) > 8 else frame.epoch)
    axes[0].legend(frameon=False)
    save(fig, path)
In [28]:
def _epoch(model, loader, device, optimizer=None):
    total_loss, labels, predictions = 0.0, [], []
    context = torch.enable_grad() if optimizer is not None else torch.no_grad()
    with context:
        for inputs, targets in loader:
            inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
            if optimizer is not None:
                optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            logits = model(inputs)
            loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, targets)
            if not torch.isfinite(loss):
                raise RuntimeError("Non-finite loss; inspect data and learning rate")
            if optimizer is not None:
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
            total_loss += loss.item() * len(targets)
            labels.extend(targets.detach().cpu().tolist())
            predictions.extend(logits.detach().argmax(1).cpu().tolist())
    if not labels:
        raise ValueError("Empty data loader")
    result = calculate_metrics(labels, predictions)
    return {"loss": total_loss / len(labels), **{k: result[k] for k in ("accuracy", "f1_macro")}}
In [29]:
def train(run: str, config: Experiment, manifest_path: Path, output_dir: Path,
          root: Path = ROOT, resume=False, skip_complete=False):
    seed_everything(config.seed)
    device = select_device(config.device)
    manifest_path, output_dir = Path(manifest_path), Path(output_dir)
    frame = pd.read_csv(manifest_path)
    verify_content(frame, root)
    manifest_hash = sha256_file(manifest_path)
    status_path = output_dir / "status.json"
    if status_path.exists():
        status = json.loads(status_path.read_text())
        same = status["config"] == config.to_dict() and status["manifest_sha256"] == manifest_hash
        if not same:
            raise ValueError("Existing run has different config or data. Use a new run/output directory")
        if status["state"] == "complete":
            if skip_complete and (output_dir / "best.pt").is_file():
                LOG.info("Skipping completed run %s", run)
                return status
            raise ValueError("Run is already complete. Use --skip-complete or a new run name")
        if not resume:
            raise ValueError("Incomplete run exists; use --resume or a new run name")
    elif resume:
        raise ValueError("Nothing to resume: status.json is missing")
    elif output_dir.exists() and any(output_dir.iterdir()):
        raise ValueError("Output directory is nonempty; choose a new run name")
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    continuing = resume and (output_dir / "last.pt").is_file()
    model = build_model(config.model, pretrained=config.pretrained and not continuing,
                        freeze_backbone=config.freeze_backbone).to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW([p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad],
                                 lr=config.lr, weight_decay=config.weight_decay)
    history, best, bad, best_epoch, start, elapsed = [], -1.0, 0, 0, 1, 0.0
    if continuing:
        saved = torch.load(output_dir / "last.pt", map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        if saved["config"] != config.to_dict() or saved["manifest_sha256"] != manifest_hash:
            raise ValueError("Resume checkpoint config/data mismatch")
        model.load_state_dict(saved["model_state"])
        optimizer.load_state_dict(saved["optimizer_state"])
        # Optimizer state tensors must follow parameters to the selected device.
        for state in optimizer.state.values():
            for key, value in state.items():
                if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor) and key != "step":
                    state[key] = value.to(device)
        history, best, bad = saved["history"], saved["best_score"], saved["bad_epochs"]
        best_epoch, start, elapsed = saved["best_epoch"], saved["epoch"] + 1, saved["training_seconds"]
    metadata = {"run": run, "config": config.to_dict(), "manifest_sha256": manifest_hash,
                "environment": environment(device), "command": sys.argv,
                "pretrained_weights": ({"mobilenet": "MobileNet_V2_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1",
                                         "convnext": "ConvNeXt_Tiny_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1"}.get(config.model)
                                       if config.pretrained else None),
                "selection": "maximum validation macro-F1; earliest epoch wins ties",
                "source_sha256": dict(SOURCE_SHA256),
                "implementation": "Notebook-local definitions from the pinned canonical source",
                "timestamp_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), **parameter_counts(model)}
    write_json(status_path, metadata | {"state": "running"})
    train_data = WeatherDataset(frame, root, "train", config.augment, config.model)
    val_data = WeatherDataset(frame, root, "val", False, config.model)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_data, batch_size=config.batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=config.num_workers)
    for epoch in range(start, config.epochs + 1):
        if bad >= config.patience:
            break
        # Absolute epoch seeds make restart reproducible; shuffle RNG is independent
        # of augmentation RNG. ConvNeXt's head is linear with no dropout.
        seed_everything(config.seed + epoch)
        generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(config.seed + epoch)
        train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=config.batch_size, shuffle=True,
                                  generator=generator, num_workers=config.num_workers)
        synchronize(device)
        started = time.perf_counter()
        set_training_mode(model, config.model, config.freeze_backbone)
        tr = _epoch(model, train_loader, device, optimizer)
        model.eval()
        va = _epoch(model, val_loader, device)
        synchronize(device)
        duration = time.perf_counter() - started
        elapsed += duration
        row = {"epoch": epoch, "seconds": duration,
               **{f"train_{k}": v for k, v in tr.items()}, **{f"val_{k}": v for k, v in va.items()}}
        history.append(row)
        improved = va["f1_macro"] > best
        if improved:
            best, bad, best_epoch = va["f1_macro"], 0, epoch
        else:
            bad += 1
        checkpoint = {"format_version": 1, "classes": list(CLASSES), "run": run,
                      "config": config.to_dict(), "manifest_sha256": manifest_hash,
                      "model_state": {k: v.detach().cpu().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()},
                      "optimizer_state": optimizer.state_dict(), "epoch": epoch, "history": history,
                      "best_score": best, "bad_epochs": bad, "best_epoch": best_epoch,
                      "training_seconds": elapsed, "metadata": metadata}
        if improved:
            atomic_checkpoint(output_dir / "best.pt", checkpoint)
        atomic_checkpoint(output_dir / "last.pt", checkpoint)
        pd.DataFrame(history).to_csv(output_dir / "history.csv", index=False)
        LOG.info("%s epoch %d/%d train loss %.4f val F1 %.4f (%0.1fs)",
                 run, epoch, config.epochs, tr["loss"], va["f1_macro"], duration)
    training_curves(history, output_dir / "training_curves.png")
    result = metadata | {"state": "complete", "epochs_ran": len(history),
                         "best_epoch": best_epoch, "best_val_f1_macro": best,
                         "training_seconds": elapsed, "stopped_early": len(history) < config.epochs,
                         "stop_reason": "early_stopping" if bad >= config.patience else "epoch_limit"}
    write_json(status_path, result)
    return result

if REPRODUCTION_OUTPUTS.resolve() == OFFICIAL_OUTPUTS.resolve() or OFFICIAL_OUTPUTS.resolve().is_relative_to(REPRODUCTION_OUTPUTS.resolve()):
    raise ValueError("Reproduction must use a separate output directory")


def reproduce_training(run):
    if not RUN_FULL_REPRODUCTION:
        return
    destination = REPRODUCTION_OUTPUTS / run
    continuing = RESUME_REPRODUCTION and (destination / "status.json").is_file()
    return train(run, configs[run], manifest_path, destination, ROOT,
                 resume=continuing, skip_complete=True)


def show_saved_experiment(run, show_matrix=True):
    directory = OFFICIAL_OUTPUTS / run
    history = pd.read_csv(directory / "history.csv")
    selected = history.loc[history.val_f1_macro.idxmax()]
    result = json.loads((directory / "test_metrics.json").read_text())
    assert int(selected.epoch) == result["best_epoch"]
    display(Markdown(f"**{EXPERIMENT_LABELS[run]}**"))
    display(history.style.hide(axis="index").format({column:"{:.4f}" for column in history if column not in ["epoch","seconds"]} | {"seconds":"{:.2f}"}))
    display(IPImage(filename=str(directory / "training_curves.png"), width=860, alt=f"Training and validation loss, accuracy and macro-F1 for {EXPERIMENT_LABELS[run]}"))
    if show_matrix:
        display(IPImage(filename=str(directory / "confusion_matrix.png"), width=460, alt=f"Test confusion matrix for {EXPERIMENT_LABELS[run]}"))
    report = pd.DataFrame(result["per_class"]).T.loc[list(CLASSES), ["precision","recall","f1-score","support"]]
    report.index = report.index.str.title()
    display(report.style.format({"precision":"{:.4f}","recall":"{:.4f}","f1-score":"{:.4f}","support":"{:.0f}"}))

Part 10 - Assignment 2: ConvNeXt-Tiny¶

ConvNeXt-Tiny (2022) is a CNN with a 4×4 stride-four stem and four stages containing 3, 3, 9 and 3 blocks. Channels grow 96→192→384→768 as resolution decreases. Each block uses a 7×7 depthwise convolution, LayerNorm, channel expansion/contraction, GELU and a scaled residual connection. Global average pooling and the pretrained final normalization feed a new Linear(768, 4) head.

The explicit adaptation below unfolds the same ConvNeXt branch already visible in build_model. Fresh training uses official ImageNet-1K V1 weights; demonstration restores every weight from the trained checkpoint. The entire backbone and normalization remain frozen; only 3,076 head parameters train. Input preprocessing remains resize 236, center crop 224 and ImageNet normalization.

Part 11 - Assignment 2 Training¶

The augmented ConvNeXt configuration uses batch size 16, learning rate 0.001, cross-entropy and AdamW, with a six-epoch limit. Validation macro-F1 selects epoch 3. The official test result is 98.18% accuracy and 0.9827 macro-F1. The same visible training controller handles the frozen feature extractor and the trainable head.

Part 12 - Augmentation Ablation Study¶

The two ConvNeXt configurations differ only in augment: architecture, pretrained weights, initialization protocol, seed, split, optimizer, batch size, epoch limit and validation-selection rule match. Each independently selects its checkpoint by validation macro-F1. The original initial-head tensors were not archived, so the controlled configuration is not direct evidence of historical initial-tensor identity.

The augmented run predicts 162/165 correctly; without augmentation it predicts 161/165. The difference is one image, not evidence of statistical significance. Cloudy and Shine F1 increase, Rain is unchanged and Sunrise F1 decreases.

Part 13 - Model Evaluation¶

The full evaluation implementation below loads the validation-selected checkpoint, verifies the fixed test membership, computes probabilities and classification metrics, exports per-image predictions, measures latency and builds the comparison. It is called only on the separate reproduction directory. Demonstration reconstructs all four official metric sets from saved predictions and can optionally verify every prediction through read-only test inference.

In [38]:
def confusion_figure(matrix, path, title="Held-out test predictions"):
    matrix = np.asarray(matrix)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.6, 4.1), layout="constrained")
    im = ax.imshow(matrix, cmap="Blues", vmin=0)
    for i in range(4):
        for j in range(4):
            ax.text(j, i, str(matrix[i, j]), ha="center", va="center",
                    color="white" if matrix[i, j] > matrix.max() * .55 else "#182B37")
    ax.set(xticks=range(4), yticks=range(4), xticklabels=LABELS, yticklabels=LABELS,
           xlabel="Predicted category", ylabel="True category", title=title)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=.8, label="Images")
    save(fig, path)


def comparison_figure(frame, path):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.6), layout="constrained")
    for ax, metric, title in zip(axes, ["accuracy", "f1_macro"], ["Test accuracy", "Test macro-F1"]):
        bars = ax.bar(frame.run, frame[metric], color=COLORS[:len(frame)])
        ax.set(ylabel=title, ylim=(0, 1.08))
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=30, labelsize=8)
        ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.3f", padding=3, fontsize=8)
    save(fig, path)

def evaluate_run(run, manifest_path, output_root, root=ROOT, device_name="auto", warmup=5, repeats=30):
    seed_everything(42)
    device = select_device(device_name)
    run_dir = Path(output_root) / run
    status = json.loads((run_dir / "status.json").read_text())
    if status["state"] != "complete":
        raise ValueError(f"Training incomplete: {run}")
    frame = pd.read_csv(manifest_path)
    verify_content(frame, root)
    model, checkpoint = load_checkpoint(run_dir / "best.pt", device)
    if checkpoint["manifest_sha256"] != sha256_file(manifest_path):
        raise ValueError("Evaluation manifest differs from training manifest")
    data = WeatherDataset(frame, root, "test", False, checkpoint["config"]["model"])
    loader = DataLoader(data, batch_size=checkpoint["config"]["batch_size"], shuffle=False, num_workers=0)
    probabilities, targets = [], []
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for x, y in loader:
            probabilities.extend(model(x.to(device)).softmax(1).cpu().tolist())
            targets.extend(y.tolist())
    predictions = np.argmax(probabilities, axis=1).tolist()
    metrics = calculate_metrics(targets, predictions)
    latency = benchmark(model, data[0][0].unsqueeze(0), device, warmup, repeats)
    prediction_frame = data.frame[["path", "label", "class_id", "group"]].copy()
    prediction_frame["predicted_class_id"] = predictions
    prediction_frame["predicted_label"] = [CLASSES[p] for p in predictions]
    prediction_frame["correct"] = prediction_frame.class_id == prediction_frame.predicted_class_id
    for j, label in enumerate(CLASSES):
        prediction_frame[f"score_{label}"] = [p[j] for p in probabilities]
    test_hash = __import__("hashlib").sha256("\n".join(data.frame.path).encode()).hexdigest()
    metrics.update(run=run, split="test", test_samples=len(data), test_membership_sha256=test_hash,
                   manifest_sha256=checkpoint["manifest_sha256"], checkpoint_sha256=sha256_file(run_dir / "best.pt"),
                   best_epoch=checkpoint["best_epoch"], latency=latency)
    prediction_frame.to_csv(run_dir / "test_predictions.csv", index=False)
    write_json(run_dir / "test_metrics.json", metrics)
    confusion_figure(metrics["confusion_matrix"], run_dir / "confusion_matrix.png")
    return metrics

def compare_runs(runs, output_root, ablation=("convnext_aug", "convnext_noaug")):
    output_root = Path(output_root)
    rows, membership, manifests = [], set(), set()
    for run in runs:
        directory = output_root / run
        metrics = json.loads((directory / "test_metrics.json").read_text())
        status = json.loads((directory / "status.json").read_text())
        if metrics["checkpoint_sha256"] != sha256_file(directory / "best.pt"):
            raise ValueError(f"Stale evaluation for {run}")
        membership.add(metrics["test_membership_sha256"])
        manifests.add(metrics["manifest_sha256"])
        rows.append({"run": run, "model": status["config"]["model"], "augment": status["config"]["augment"],
                     **{key: metrics[key] for key in ["accuracy", "precision_macro", "recall_macro", "f1_macro", "test_samples"]},
                     "latency_mean_ms": metrics["latency"]["mean_ms"],
                     "latency_median_ms": metrics["latency"]["median_ms"],
                     "parameters": status["parameters"], "trainable_parameters": status["trainable_parameters"],
                     "training_seconds": status["training_seconds"], "best_epoch": status["best_epoch"],
                     "validation_f1_macro": status["best_val_f1_macro"],
                     "device": metrics["latency"]["environment"]["device"]})
    if len(membership) != 1 or len(manifests) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Cannot compare models with different dataset/test membership")
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    frame.to_csv(output_root / "model_comparison.csv", index=False)
    comparison_figure(frame, output_root / "model_comparison.png")
    if set(ablation).issubset(set(runs)):
        configs = [Experiment(**json.loads((output_root / run / "status.json").read_text())["config"]) for run in ablation]
        validate_ablation(*configs)
        subset = frame.set_index("run").loc[list(ablation)].reset_index()
        subset.to_csv(output_root / "ablation.csv", index=False)
        delta = float(subset.iloc[0].f1_macro - subset.iloc[1].f1_macro)
        write_json(output_root / "ablation_analysis.json", {
            "comparison": "augmentation minus no augmentation", "test_f1_macro_delta": delta,
            "interpretation": f"Augmentation {'increased' if delta > 0 else 'decreased' if delta < 0 else 'did not change'} test macro-F1 by {abs(delta):.4f} under the shared evaluation protocol.",
            "control": "All serialized configuration fields except augment are identical; identical manifest and test membership verified",
            "selection": "Each configuration selected its own best validation macro-F1 checkpoint; no test-based tuning"})
    return frame

Part 14 - Grad-CAM¶

Grad-CAM differentiates a selected class logit with respect to spatial activations. Mean gradients form channel weights; the positive weighted activation sum is resized and normalized. The final ConvNeXt stage is 768×7×7; an earlier 384×14×14 stage is an experimental alternative. Input gradients allow attribution through frozen weights without updating parameter gradients. Hooks and module modes are restored even on failure.

The mapping and overlay code inverts the actual resize/center crop and leaves unseen pixels unchanged. Bright colors indicate relative positive attribution, not cloud segmentation or causal proof. An error is explained for the predicted class, not automatically its dataset label.

In [43]:
TARGET_STAGES = {"final":7, "earlier":5}

def gradcam_convnext(model, x, target=None, layer="final", return_details=False):
    """Grad-CAM of a class logit, with the original final-stage default.

    alpha_k = mean_ij(d logit_c / d A_kij); L = ReLU(sum_k alpha_k A_k).
    Bilinear interpolation is followed by the existing within-map min/max scale.
    Earlier-stage maps are complementary attributions, not equivalent resolutions.
    """
    import operator
    from torchvision.models.convnext import ConvNeXt
    if not isinstance(model, ConvNeXt) or layer not in TARGET_STAGES:
        raise ValueError("Choose final or earlier on a TorchVision ConvNeXt model")
    if x.ndim != 4 or tuple(x.shape[:2]) != (1, 3) or min(x.shape[-2:]) < 32:
        raise ValueError("Grad-CAM expects one RGB NCHW input image")
    if not x.is_floating_point() or not torch.isfinite(x).all():
        raise ValueError("Grad-CAM input must contain finite floating-point values")
    if target is not None:
        try:
            if isinstance(target, (bool, np.bool_)):
                raise TypeError
            target = operator.index(target)
        except TypeError as error:
            raise ValueError("Target class must be an integer in [0, 3]") from error
        if target not in range(4):
            raise ValueError("Target class must be in [0, 3]")
    captured = []
    stage = model.features[TARGET_STAGES[layer]]
    handle = stage.register_forward_hook(lambda module, inputs, output: captured.append(output))
    modes = [(module, module.training) for module in model.modules()]
    model.eval()
    try:
        # Also works when the caller entered inference_mode. Only the cloned input
        # gains a graph; autograd.grad does not populate parameter .grad buffers.
        with torch.inference_mode(False), torch.enable_grad():
            inputs = x.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
            logits = model(inputs)
            if logits.shape != (1, 4) or not torch.isfinite(logits).all():
                raise ValueError("Grad-CAM requires four finite class logits")
            index = int(logits.argmax(1).item()) if target is None else target
            if len(captured) != 1 or captured[0].ndim != 4:
                raise ValueError("Target stage must return one spatial NCHW activation")
            activation = captured[0]
            gradient = torch.autograd.grad(logits[0, index], activation)[0]
            if not torch.isfinite(activation).all() or not torch.isfinite(gradient).all():
                raise ValueError("Non-finite Grad-CAM activations or gradients")
            weights = gradient.mean(dim=(2, 3), keepdim=True)
            native = F.relu((weights * activation).sum(1, keepdim=True))
            heatmap = F.interpolate(native, size=inputs.shape[-2:], mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)[0, 0]
            heatmap = heatmap - heatmap.min()
            peak = heatmap.max()
            if peak > 0:
                heatmap = heatmap / peak
            result = heatmap.detach().cpu().numpy()
            if not return_details:
                return result
            return result, {"target_class": index, "target_logit": float(logits[0, index].detach().cpu()),
                            "target_layer": f"features[{TARGET_STAGES[layer]}]", "stage": layer,
                            "activation_shape": list(activation.shape), "gradient_shape": list(gradient.shape),
                            "native_heatmap": native[0, 0].detach().cpu().numpy(),
                            "gradient_abs_max": float(gradient.abs().max().detach().cpu()),
                            "spatially_constant": bool(peak == 0),
                            "normalization": "ReLU; bilinear resize, align_corners=False; subtract min then divide by max if positive"}
    finally:
        handle.remove()
        # Restore every flag, including a training head with an eval-mode backbone.
        for module, training in modes:
            module.training = training

def map_heatmap_to_original(original, heatmap, architecture="convnext"):
    """Invert resize/center-crop geometry; zero attribution outside crop bounds.

    The geometric field of view is defined at original-pixel centers. Resampling
    may otherwise bleed a fractional tint beyond its edge.
    """
    values = np.asarray(heatmap, dtype=np.float32)
    if values.shape != (224, 224) or not np.isfinite(values).all() or values.min() < 0 or values.max() > 1:
        raise ValueError("Heatmap must be finite, normalized to [0, 1], and 224 by 224")
    if original.width * original.height > 25_000_000 or max(original.size) / min(original.size) > 64:
        raise ValueError("Use an image under 25 megapixels and an aspect ratio at most 64:1")
    resized = TF.resize(original, resize_size(architecture))
    width, height = resized.size
    left, top = int(round((width - 224) / 2)), int(round((height - 224) / 2))
    canvas = Image.new("F", (width, height), 0)
    canvas.paste(Image.fromarray(values), (left, top))
    mapped = np.asarray(canvas.resize(original.size, Image.Resampling.BILINEAR)).copy().clip(0, 1)
    y, x = np.ogrid[:original.height, :original.width]
    visible = (((x + .5) * width / original.width >= left) & ((x + .5) * width / original.width < left + 224)
               & ((y + .5) * height / original.height >= top) & ((y + .5) * height / original.height < top + 224))
    mapped[~visible] = 0
    return mapped
In [45]:
def heatmap_image(heatmap):
    """Inferno rendering of unchanged normalized attribution values."""
    values = np.asarray(heatmap)
    if values.ndim != 2 or not np.isfinite(values).all() or values.min() < 0 or values.max() > 1:
        raise ValueError("Heatmap must be a finite normalized 2D array")
    return Image.fromarray(np.rint(plt.get_cmap("inferno")(values)[..., :3] * 255).astype(np.uint8))


def overlay_image(original, heatmap, architecture="convnext", alpha=0.40):
    """Strength-weighted overlay; alpha changes display only, never attribution."""
    if not np.isfinite(alpha) or not 0 <= alpha <= 1:
        raise ValueError("Overlay opacity must be between zero and one")
    original = original.convert("RGB")
    mapped = map_heatmap_to_original(original, heatmap, architecture)
    pixels = np.asarray(original)
    result = pixels.copy()
    # Bound colormap/blending temporaries for large accepted photographs.
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("inferno")
    for top in range(0, original.height, 128):
        values = mapped[top:top + 128]
        active = alpha * values > 0
        if active.any():
            opacity = (alpha * values[active])[:, None]
            color = cmap(values[active])[:, :3]
            source = pixels[top:top + 128][active]
            blended = source * (1 - opacity) + color * 255 * opacity
            result[top:top + 128][active] = np.rint(blended).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return Image.fromarray(result)

def generate_examples(run_dir, manifest_path, root=ROOT, count=6, device_name="auto"):
    import json
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    predictions = pd.read_csv(run_dir / "test_predictions.csv")
    metrics = json.loads((run_dir / "test_metrics.json").read_text())
    if metrics["manifest_sha256"] != sha256_file(manifest_path):
        raise ValueError("Grad-CAM manifest differs from evaluation")
    if metrics["checkpoint_sha256"] != sha256_file(run_dir / "best.pt"):
        raise ValueError("Checkpoint changed after evaluation")
    device = select_device(device_name)
    model, checkpoint = load_checkpoint(run_dir / "best.pt", device)
    if checkpoint["config"]["model"] != "convnext":
        raise ValueError("Grad-CAM examples require ConvNeXt")
    # Deterministic post-evaluation selection includes errors when available.
    wrong = predictions[predictions.class_id != predictions.predicted_class_id]
    right = predictions[predictions.class_id == predictions.predicted_class_id]
    selected = pd.concat([wrong.head(max(1, count // 2)), right.head(count)]).head(count)
    selected.to_csv(run_dir / "gradcam_examples.csv", index=False)
    records = []
    for i, row in enumerate(selected.itertuples()):
        original = open_rgb(root / row.path)
        tensor = transform(architecture="convnext")(original).unsqueeze(0).to(device)
        cam = gradcam_convnext(model, tensor, row.predicted_class_id)
        np.save(run_dir / f"gradcam_{i + 1:02d}.npy", cam)
        overlay = overlay_image(original, cam)
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.5, 3.5), layout="constrained")
        axes[0].imshow(original)
        axes[0].set_title(f"Original · true: {row.label.title()}", fontsize=10)
        axes[1].imshow(overlay)
        axes[1].set_title(f"Grad-CAM · predicted: {row.predicted_label.title()}", fontsize=10)
        for ax in axes:
            ax.axis("off")
        name = f"gradcam_{i + 1:02d}.png"
        save(fig, run_dir / name)
        records.append({"figure": name, "path": row.path, "true": row.label,
                        "predicted": row.predicted_label, "correct": row.label == row.predicted_label,
                        "heatmap_min": float(cam.min()), "heatmap_max": float(cam.max())})
    write_json(run_dir / "gradcam_metadata.json", {"target_layer": "features[-1] (final spatial stage, before pooling)",
               "checkpoint_sha256": metrics["checkpoint_sha256"], "examples": records,
               "errors_available": len(wrong), "note": "Post-evaluation examples; approximate feature attribution, not segmentation or causal proof. Original image preserved; center-crop mapping inverted for overlay."})
    return records

Part 15 - Explainability Validation¶

The completed diagnostic uses 22 held-out images: four seeded correct cases per class, all three errors and all six original explanation examples, with repeated IDs removed. Each 224-square input is split into a 7×7 grid. High, low and ten random controls each remove five 32-square cells (10.20% of visible pixels), holding the original predicted class fixed. Replacement is either normalized mean fill or Gaussian blur. The score is original target logit minus perturbed target logit. Random masks share the same image seed across layers and baselines.

The functions below implement the region selection and batched interventions. The following runner includes the actual sample-selection and aggregation procedure; optional reruns write only to the notebook work directory. The historical summary is reconstructed from its 1,056 saved records, not replaced by the small live CPU illustration.

In [48]:
def region_selections(heatmap, grid=7, count=5, random_repeats=10, seed=42):
    cam = np.asarray(heatmap, dtype=np.float32)
    if cam.shape != (224, 224) or not np.isfinite(cam).all() or cam.min() < 0 or cam.max() > 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected a finite normalized 224-square heatmap')
    if not isinstance(grid, int) or grid < 2 or 224 % grid or not 1 <= count <= grid * grid // 2:
        raise ValueError('Choose an equal-size grid dividing 224 and a valid region budget')
    if not isinstance(random_repeats, int) or random_repeats < 1:
        raise ValueError('At least one random control is required')
    side = 224 // grid
    importance = cam.reshape(grid, side, grid, side).mean(axis=(1, 3)).reshape(-1)
    # Stable tie-breaking by row-major region ID is recorded for constant maps.
    order = np.argsort(importance, kind='stable')
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    selected = [('high', order[-count:][::-1].tolist()), ('low', order[:count].tolist())]
    selected += [('random', rng.choice(grid * grid, count, replace=False).tolist()) for _ in range(random_repeats)]
    return importance, selected

def occlusion_check(model, x, heatmap, target, *, baseline='mean', grid=7, count=5,
                    random_repeats=10, seed=42, batch_size=6):
    if x.shape != (1, 3, 224, 224) or not x.is_floating_point() or not torch.isfinite(x).all():
        raise ValueError('Expected one finite normalized RGB tensor of shape (1,3,224,224)')
    try:
        if isinstance(target, (bool, np.bool_)):
            raise TypeError
        target = operator.index(target)
    except TypeError as error:
        raise ValueError('Target must be an integer class index') from error
    if target not in range(4) or baseline not in {'mean', 'blur'} or batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError('Invalid target, baseline or batch size')
    importance, selected = region_selections(heatmap, grid, count, random_repeats, seed)
    side = 224 // grid
    modes = [(m, m.training) for m in model.modules()]
    model.eval()
    try:
        with torch.inference_mode():
            original = model(x)[0]
            if original.shape != (4,) or not torch.isfinite(original).all():
                raise ValueError('Expected four finite logits')
            replacement = torch.zeros_like(x) if baseline == 'mean' else gaussian_blur(x, [31, 31], [10., 10.])
            variants = []
            for _, regions in selected:
                changed = x.clone()
                for region in regions:
                    row, column = divmod(region, grid)
                    ys, xs = slice(row * side, (row + 1) * side), slice(column * side, (column + 1) * side)
                    changed[:, :, ys, xs] = replacement[:, :, ys, xs]
                variants.append(changed[0])
            scores = torch.cat([model(torch.stack(variants[i:i+batch_size])) for i in range(0, len(variants), batch_size)])
            if not torch.isfinite(scores).all():
                raise ValueError('Non-finite occluded logits')
            original_logit = float(original[target].cpu())
            original_probability = float(original.softmax(0)[target].cpu())
            scores, probabilities = scores.cpu(), scores.softmax(1).cpu()
        rows = []
        for i, (control, regions) in enumerate(selected):
            rows.append({'control': control, 'random_repeat': i - 2 if control == 'random' else None,
                         'regions': regions, 'occluded_pixels': count * side * side,
                         'occluded_fraction': count / grid ** 2, 'target_class': target,
                         'original_logit': original_logit, 'occluded_logit': float(scores[i, target]),
                         'logit_drop': original_logit - float(scores[i, target]),
                         'original_probability': original_probability,
                         'occluded_probability': float(probabilities[i, target]),
                         'probability_drop': original_probability - float(probabilities[i, target]),
                         'occluded_predicted_class': int(scores[i].argmax())})
        return {'target_class': target, 'baseline': baseline, 'seed': seed, 'grid': grid,
                'region_count': count, 'random_repeats': random_repeats,
                'spatially_constant_map': bool(importance.max() == importance.min()),
                'region_importance': importance.tolist(), 'rows': rows}
    finally:
        for module, training in modes:
            module.training = training

def run_explanation_validation(device_name="auto", output_dir=WORK_DIR / "explainability_validation"):
    seed_everything(42);device=select_device(device_name);directory=Path(output_dir);directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True,parents=True)
    predictions=pd.read_csv(ROOT/'outputs/convnext_aug/test_predictions.csv')
    rng=np.random.default_rng(42);chosen=[]
    for label in ['cloudy','rain','shine','sunrise']:
        candidates=predictions[(predictions.label==label)&(predictions.class_id==predictions.predicted_class_id)]
        chosen.extend(candidates.iloc[rng.choice(len(candidates),4,replace=False)].path.tolist())
    chosen.extend(predictions[predictions.class_id!=predictions.predicted_class_id].path)
    chosen.extend(pd.read_csv(ROOT/'outputs/convnext_aug/gradcam_examples.csv').path)
    chosen=list(dict.fromkeys(chosen));samples=predictions.set_index('path').loc[chosen].reset_index()
    samples.to_csv(directory/'samples.csv',index=False)
    model,_=load_checkpoint(ROOT/'outputs/convnext_aug/best.pt',device)
    before={name:p.detach().cpu().clone() for name,p in model.state_dict().items()};records=[];maps=[];start=time.perf_counter()
    for i,row in enumerate(samples.itertuples()):
        image=open_rgb(ROOT/row.path);x=transform(architecture='convnext')(image).unsqueeze(0).to(device)
        with torch.inference_mode(): assert int(model(x).argmax())==row.predicted_class_id
        for layer in ['final','earlier']:
            cam,details=gradcam_convnext(model,x,row.predicted_class_id,layer,True)
            native=details.pop('native_heatmap');name=f'{i:02d}_{Path(row.path).stem}_{layer}'
            np.savez_compressed(directory/f'{name}.npz',heatmap=cam,native=native)
            maps.append({'path':row.path,'correct':bool(row.correct),'label':row.label,'predicted':row.predicted_label,
                         'file':name+'.npz',**details,'peak_yx_224':list(map(int,np.unravel_index(cam.argmax(),cam.shape))),
                         'bottom_third_mass_fraction':float(cam[149:].sum()/cam.sum()) if cam.sum() else 0})
            for baseline in ['mean','blur']:
                result=occlusion_check(model,x,cam,row.predicted_class_id,baseline=baseline,seed=42+i)
                for r in result['rows']:
                    records.append({'path':row.path,'label':row.label,'predicted':row.predicted_label,'correct':bool(row.correct),
                                    'layer':layer,'baseline':baseline,'seed':42+i,**r})
        print(f'{i+1}/{len(samples)} {Path(row.path).name}',flush=True)
    assert all(torch.equal(p.detach().cpu(),before[name]) for name,p in model.state_dict().items())
    assert not model.training and all(p.grad is None for p in model.parameters())
    frame=pd.DataFrame(records)
    csv=frame.copy()
    csv['regions']=csv.regions.map(json.dumps)
    csv.to_csv(directory/'scores.csv',index=False)
    # Each image has equal weight; first average its 10 random controls.
    paired=frame.groupby(['path','layer','baseline','control'],sort=False).logit_drop.mean().unstack('control').reset_index()
    paired.to_csv(directory/'paired_scores.csv',index=False);summary=[]
    for (layer,baseline),group in paired.groupby(['layer','baseline']):
        summary.append({'layer':layer,'baseline':baseline,'samples':len(group),
                        **{control+'_mean_logit_drop':float(group[control].mean()) for control in ['high','low','random']},
                        'high_gt_low_count':int((group.high>group.low).sum()),'high_gt_random_count':int((group.high>group.random).sum()),
                        'high_minus_low_median':float((group.high-group.low).median())})
    pd.DataFrame(summary).to_csv(directory/'summary.csv',index=False)
    write_json(directory/'settings.json',{'checkpoint_sha256':sha256_file(ROOT/'outputs/convnext_aug/best.pt'),'manifest_sha256':sha256_file(ROOT/'data/manifest.csv'),
       'environment':environment(device),'selection':'Seed 42: four saved-correct test images per class, all three saved errors, plus all six existing Grad-CAM examples; duplicates removed. Enriched diagnostic sample, not a population estimate.',
       'sample_count':len(samples),'layers':{'final':'features[7]: 768x7x7','earlier':'features[5]: 384x14x14'},'occlusion':{'grid':[7,7],'cell_pixels':[32,32],'cells_removed':5,'fraction':5/49,'random_repeats':10,'seed':'42 + fixed sample row index','target':'original predicted class, held fixed after perturbation','mean_baseline':'normalized zeros = ImageNet RGB mean [0.485,0.456,0.406]','blur_baseline':'Gaussian blur of the same normalized input; kernel31, sigma10; replace only selected cells'},
       'map_settings':maps,'parameter_mutation':False,'seconds':time.perf_counter()-start})
    fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(10,4),layout='constrained')
    for ax,baseline in zip(axes,['mean','blur']):
        for j,layer in enumerate(['final','earlier']):
            part=paired[(paired.baseline==baseline)&(paired.layer==layer)]
            for k,control in enumerate(['high','low','random']):
                x=j*4+k;values=part[control].to_numpy();ax.bar(x,values.mean(),color=['#21635D','#9E7560','#5B7395'][k],width=.7)
                ax.scatter(np.full(len(values),x)+np.linspace(-.2,.2,len(values)),values,s=11,c='#263D35',alpha=.65,zorder=3)
        ax.set(xticks=[0,1,2,4,5,6],xticklabels=['High','Low','Random']*2,ylabel='Original target logit − occluded logit',title=f'{baseline.title()} replacement; 5 of 49 equal cells')
        ax.axhline(0,c='#7A8F84',lw=.7);ax.text(.23,-.17,'Final stage',transform=ax.transAxes,ha='center');ax.text(.77,-.17,'Earlier stage',transform=ax.transAxes,ha='center')
    fig.savefig(directory/'occlusion_comparison.png',dpi=250,bbox_inches='tight');plt.close(fig)
